historical_commentary.text: Positioned as an introductory primer, this note covers the basic architecture of ODBC and how 4D 2004's new native ODBC features fit into it, intended for readers new to ODBC as well as those familiar with the standard but unfamiliar with using it from 4th Dimension. ODBC as a general database connectivity standard remains in active use today, so the conceptual grounding this primer provides is still broadly valid, but the specific 4D 2004 feature set it describes has been superseded by two decades of subsequent 4D data-access evolution.
related_updates: 4D's own native SQL engine (from 4D v11 SQL, ~2007) reduced the centrality of ODBC for internal data access
ORDA (2018) introduced a modern entity-based data access model that supplements or replaces ODBC-style access for many use cases
ODBC itself remains a widely supported standard, but the specific 4D 2004 native ODBC feature set described here has been substantially revised in later 4D versions
